not_checked: held_out checks printed sample counts on distinct row indices, not an iris model score. stratified applies the printed first-fold counts as a one-third hold-out; it does not claim the identical random split. grouped checks the printed test folds (sorted, and in the printed order at seed 0, where G6's seeded shuffle deals them so; the source's folds are unshuffled), and the case author's reading of them: sorted sizes, partition and disjointness with one group per fold. grouped_hold_out checks make_split's keeping of identical rows on one side of the hold-out split on rows in identical pairs.

Property-checked, because the source prints no worked value G6's functions can be run on: cv_training_part runs the rank path (_fit._rank, which cross-validates with cross_validate inside the training rows and reads the held-out rows only to predict them) with one dummy-regressor candidate, comparing its fold scores with an independent fold mean absolute error and checking that different held-out rows change none of them; with one candidate, nothing is chosen between candidates. preprocessing_in_pipeline (its 50-category cap G6's own choice, which holds this certificate at qualified-draft) fits through _fit.fit_predict twice with different held-out rows and compares the fitted transformation of the training rows; generated inputs compare numeric imputation and scaling with independent array algebra. seed checks the integer random_state passed to an actual G6-created decision tree, not the source's RandomState score. baseline compares majority and mean predictions: the source prints 0.579, its most-frequent baseline's score, for a split of the bundled iris data whose labels it does not print, so there is no printed value G6's baseline function can be run on. balanced_accuracy and headline_imbalance compare independent computations; the 10% headline threshold is G6's own choice (headline_imbalance is marked own_choice, which holds this certificate at qualified-draft).
The source's caveat that an integer seed 'may lead to less robust cross-validation results' (12.3.3.2) is not checked, and the results do not say so.

rmse is squared for the printed mean squared error and compared directly with an independent square root on generated inputs. The constant-target R2 case checks only that R2 is reported undefined; generated and boundary inputs include constant non-integer targets.

rank reports the standard deviation of each candidate's fold scores from stratified folds; the source notes that stratification can artificially shrink that spread when classes are rare. The spread is not checked, and the results do not say so.

Each guard fires at its threshold, holds just inside it and fires on its recall set; G6's removal of it breaks its firing case, and a seeded change of its threshold or of a comparison at it is caught. What else its code does rests on the independent reader's word (effect_only). Their thresholds (0.99 for leakage and for a too-good headline, 10 held-out rows, the lift's interval above zero, a 0.10 gap, the text and class limits) are G6's own. Of interval, only the claim it gates is checked, not the interval's own values (its resamples, percentiles and cluster bootstrap). Of bounds, the rows to predict are held to the column and text limits in the same function (_bounds), and cases send them. overfit_gap is checked on _gap_note, the note alone, not on the reply's wording. held_out_from_rows checks the caution made from a count, not the count kept under G6_HOME.

Categorical one-hot encoding and its 50-category cap, all estimator classes, model-selection quality, request validation by the typed input (the caller rule limits) and every possible workload are not checked. The directly callable _pipeline, _estimator, folds, fit_predict and _rank functions run with scikit-learn installed.

Full rank and fit orchestration (block._rank and fit_eval) launches a further child and writes held-out usage state, so it is outside this numerical certificate; the rank path runs in the certificate's own child with one candidate.
